overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: no April 2015 or April 5, 2016 minutes existed for lack of a quorum, and the approved April 26, 2016 minutes substantially complied on accuracy.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to provide the April 13, 2015 meeting minutes upon request.
allegations.key_passage: Neither set of minutes existed at that time because less than a quorum of the nine-member Board attended the scheduled meetings on those days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to approve its April 5, 2016 meeting minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Neither set of minutes existed at that time because less than a quorum of the nine-member Board attended the scheduled meetings on those days.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 26, 2016 minutes omitted the chair's statements about a person allegedly harassing board members.
allegations.key_passage: the final minutes, approved after this complaint was filed, sufficiently summarized the discussion regarding "potential harassment" of Board members in substantial compliance with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
